mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille for Hague Convention member states; French Consular Legalization for non-member states, followed by certified French translation by an approved court translator

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Utility provider, municipal tax office, or banking institution in the country of residence
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization with certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of good standing or official register extract for any legal-entity shareholder
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Official companies registry of the legal-entity shareholder's jurisdiction of incorporation
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization with certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Bank reference letter confirming the source of funds intended for the share capital contribution
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Banking institution maintaining the UBO's funding account
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization with certified French translation

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Criminal record extract (extract No. 3 of the casier judiciaire or equivalent home-country certificate) for the proposed SAS president and any authorized manager

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille or French Consular Legalization with certified French translation

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all shareholders, ultimate beneficial owners, proposed SAS president, and signatories against (i) the EU Consolidated Financial Sanctions File under Regulation (EU) n°269/2014; (ii) the French national asset-freeze directory (gel des avoirs) maintained by the Direction Générale du Trésor; (iii) the United Nations Security Council Consolidated List; (iv) FATF high-risk jurisdiction calls; (v) OFAC SDN and sectoral sanctions lists where any pending or future transaction is USD-denominated; and (vi) national and EU political-exposed-persons (PEP) databases. Acceptable onboarding outcome requires zero un-cleared sanctions hits and fully documented economic rationale, source-of-funds evidence, and identification of each UBO holding at least 25% of capital or voting rights.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: INPI — Registre National du Commerce et des Sociétés (RCS), accessed via data.inpi.fr and the Infogreffe electronic filing platform (www.infogreffe.fr)
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: French law requires the company denomination to be written in Latin script and to be sufficiently distinctive within the RCS. A foreign-language brand name (including English brand names used by a Shopify DTC store) may be adopted as the legal corporate name provided it does not mislead the public and is transcribed in Latin characters. The official filing dossier must be drafted in French; any non-French supporting document must be accompanied by a certified French translation. The mandatory publication in a Journal d'Annonces Légales must be in French.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: France does not maintain a standalone statutory name-reservation file at the RCS; clearance is verified by the commercial court registrar at the time of filing, and the 30-day window corresponds to the legal opposition period running from the publication of the incorporation notice in a Journal d'Annonces Légales. Upon registrar rejection of the draft denomination, the incorporator or legal counsel must: (i) obtain the written refusal notice identifying the conflicting earlier right; (ii) submit an amended denomination or an added distinguishing element through the CFE/Infogreffe within 15 days of the refusal without additional registry fees; (iii) where the conflict arises from a prior trademark right of a third party, either obtain a coexistence or consent letter from the earlier mark owner or initiate an opposition procedure before the INPI within the two-month statutory time limit; (iv) for tokens requiring prior ministerial or professional authorization (e.g., ACPR authorization for banking/insurance terms), obtain the relevant regulatory clearance before refiling; and (v) in cases of arbitrary or abusive registrar refusal, file a summary adversarial application before the President of the competent Tribunal de Commerce seeking an order to register the name.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible subject to Article L.123-11-1 of the French Commercial Code. The SAS may validly fix its statutory registered office (siège social) at the premises of an authorized commercial domiciliation company (société de domiciliation) located in France. The domiciliation arrangement requires a written contract, payment of a commercial fee, and physical premises capable of receiving mail and occasionally receiving the company's representatives and agents. For a Shopify DTC e-commerce brand, the virtual office is accepted for incorporation and legal registration; however, French banks and the tax administration require demonstrable commercial substance, evidenced by management minutes, domiciliation contract terms, and, where applicable, inventory or warehousing arrangements within the EU. It is advisable to establish the management seat and principal books in France to secure French tax residence and VAT compliance under Article 209 of the Code Général des Impôts.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Low to moderate — approximately 20% probability of an unannounced on-site inspection within the first 36 months of operation. Risk drivers include (i) registrar verification of the effective registered office, (ii) tax administration control during French VAT registration or EU cross-border B2C threshold analysis, and (iii) deployment of domiciliation companies housing multiple merchants at a single address, which raises audit flags. For a pure DTC webstore without a French physical warehouse, the risk remains contained to the domiciliation address; the probability increases materially if the company claims French input VAT credits or participates in EU distance-selling thresholds.

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: French Commercial Code (Code de commerce): SAS regime, Articles L.227-1 to L.227-20; general incorporation and registration, Articles L.210-1 to L.210-9, L.224-1 to L.224-8, R.224-3 et seq.; RCS (Registre du Commerce et des Sociétés), Articles L.123-1, R.123-30.
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce (Registrar of the Commercial Court) of the registered office's jurisdiction, operating through the Guichet Unique des Formalités des Entreprises (single business formalities window) of the INPI (Institut National de la Propriété Industrielle) at formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Electronic dossier de création d'entreprise submitted via the Guichet Unique; registration produces the RCS certificate 'Extrait K-Bis' and the SIREN/SIRET numbers; the statutory Articles of Association (statuts) are annexed as the constitutive instrument.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum capital for an SAS; the Articles may validly fix capital at €1. Cash subscriptions must be paid up to at least 50% of nominal value upon subscription; the balance must be fully paid within five years of registration (Art. L.227-2, Code de commerce). All cash contributions must be escrowed in a blocked account (compte bloqué) at a French bank, the Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or a notary; funds are released to the President only upon presentation of the Extrait K-Bis. In-kind contributions are fully liberated upon subscription.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en:
FIRST BOARD RESOLUTION OF THE FOUNDING SHAREHOLDERS OF [COMPANY], SAS

The undersigned founding shareholders, having initialed the Articles of Association, hereby resolve:

1. Share Subscription. The entire share capital of €[●], divided into [●] fully paid shares, is irrevocably subscribed; subscription funds are deposited in the blocked escrow account at [Bank] pending registration.

2. Registered Office. The registered office is fixed at [●] and adopted for all corporate, tax, and administrative purposes until relocated by the President.

3. Appointments. [Name] is appointed President, with full powers to bind the company, open bank accounts, complete RCS registration, and act before courts.

This resolution is passed unanimously as the first corporate act.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Drafting and execution of the Articles of Association (Statuts)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Founders jointly (notaire optional; private deed 'acte sous seing privé' is permissible except for certain in-kind contributions or real estate contributions requiring a notary)
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Prepare the statuts setting out the corporate name, purpose (online DTC retail under ISIC 4791), registered office, share capital, share classes, and the President's powers. Execute in as many originals as parties plus one for the registry; each original must state that it is destined for RCS filing. The President must accept office in the deed.
required_dossiers: Passport/national ID and residential proof of each founder and the President
Proof of right to occupy the registered office (lease, ownership, or domiciliation agreement)
Statement of the beneficial owners for RBE filing
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If any clause is legally defective, rectify by an acte rectificatif approved unanimously by the founders and annex the rectification to the statuts before filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Deposit of share capital into blocked escrow account (compte bloqué)
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: French credit institution, Caisse des Dépôts et Consignations, or notaire acting as depositary
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Open a temporary account in the name of the company 'en formation' and transfer the cash subscriptions. Obtain the attestation de dépôt de fonds (blocking certificate) stating the amount and the depositary; the funds remain blockés until the Extrait K-Bis is issued and must never be drawn down pre-registration.
required_dossiers: KYC and beneficial-ownership forms of the depositary bank
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the bank rejects the deposit, retain a notary or the Caisse des Dépôts to receive the funds; the blocking certificate can be reissued by the substituted depositary without changing the amount.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Publication of the legal formation notice (avis de constitution) in an authorized legal announcements journal
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Authorized Journal d'Annonces Légales (JAL) in the department of the registered office
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Place the notice stating the legal form (SAS), corporate name, corporate purpose, capital, registered office, duration, and the President's identity, together with the court of registration. The JAL returns the attestation de parution certifying the publication date; the publication must precede the filing application.
required_dossiers: Identity of the applicant or its proxy
Copy of the statuts, where requested, for consistency check
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If publication is refused for non-conformity, correct the notice and republish; if the registrar later annuls publication, republish immediately with a rectificatif and annex both attestations to the registration file.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: DGFiP - Direction Generale des Finances Publiques (French General Directorate of Public Finances), Ministry of Economy, Finance and Industrial and Digital Sovereignty; taxpayer portal: impots.gouv.fr; business-formation portal (Guichet Unique): formalites.entreprises.gouv.fr; customs and export clearance: DGDDI - Direction Generale des Douanes et Droits Indirects (douane.gouv.fr); VAT identification is assigned by the local Service des Impots des Entreprises (SIE).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: Standard path for a French SAS (including 100% foreign-owned): (1) incorporate via Guichet Unique (single electronic window) submitting the articles of association, shareholder/UBO detail and the appointed president; (2) the file is transmitted to the Registre du Commerce et des Societes (RCS) through the commercial court registry; the Kbis extract is issued containing the 9-digit SIREN and SIRET, which constitute the statutory French tax identification number; (3) for a taxable activity the SIE automatically issues the intra-Community VAT number (format FR + 2-digit key + 9-digit SIREN, 13 characters in total); if not auto-issued, the company files VAT-registration form 11407 with the competent SIE; (4) a foreign company with no French registered office but with a French fixed establishment files the same Guichet Unique foreign-entity dossier and obtains a French FR VAT ID; (5) a non-EU company with no French permanent establishment selling DTC goods into France may either register directly for French VAT under art. 286 ter CGI or use the IOSS for imported consignments up to EUR 150; direct non-EU registration requires a DGFiP-accredited fiscal representative under art. 289 A CGI unless an exemption applies; (6) standard processing time is 5 to 10 working days for SIREN/SIRET, with VAT ID reference back-datable to the first taxable supply.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.default_entity_tax_classification: Entity_Level_Taxation; Territorial_Scope (territoriality principle). An SAS is mandatorily subject to corporate income tax (impot sur les societes) under arts. 206-209 CGI with no default pass-through status. Under art. 209-I CGI, only profits from activities carried on in France are taxable in France; profits of foreign permanent establishments are exempt in France unless a fiscal-integration election or treaty provision brings them into the French net. The DTC Shopify webstore is a fully taxable French commercial activity; no Tax_Exempt_Zone or Pass_Through_Eligible classification is available for this scope.
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: France has no US-style check-the-box classification; the SAS is irrebuttably taxed at entity level. Available elections: (i) fiscal integration (integration fiscale, art. 223 A CGI) - a parent holding at least 95% of the SAS may consolidate French taxable results under a firm 5-year engagement; (ii) optional pass-through for qualifying newly created SMEs under art. 239 bis AA CGI (taxation of shareholders under personal income tax during the first fiscal years, subject to strict statutory conditions and a timely filing with the SIE); (iii) VAT elections: option for the real normal regime when the franchise en base exemption applies; election of the Union One-Stop-Shop (OSS) or Import One-Stop-Shop (IOSS) to centralize EU distance-sales VAT reporting; option for the simplified real regime (regime reel simplifie) below the EUR 840,000 goods-turnover ceiling; (iv) hybrid-mismatch outcomes under art. 212 bis CGI (ATAD) are mandatory and non-elective, but the taxpayer may align financial statements and tax consolidations to invoke the tie-breaker rules avoiding double non-taxation.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Banque de France (Bank of France), operating within the Eurosystem and the European System of Central Banks; monetary policy authority for the euro is the European Central Bank, while the Banque de France administers balance-of-payments statistical reporting (SITCO), the direct-investment survey regime, and the prudential infrastructure alongside the ACPR (Autorité de Contrôle Prudentiel et de Résolution) for banking and payment-institution licensing.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: France provides full current-account and capital-account convertibility for the euro pursuant to Articles 63-65 of the Treaty on the Functioning of the European Union. There are no exchange-control authorizations, no prior permits, and no administrative limits on inbound equity injection, profit repatriation, dividend distribution, royalty payments, or intercompany loan servicing for an SAS. The practical frictions are indirect: (i) a French 25% withholding tax on dividends paid to non-resident shareholders unless reduced under an applicable double-tax treaty (e.g., 15% under the France-Singapore treaty, 10% under the France-Hong Kong treaty with conditions, 0-15% under various EU directives/treaties), and (ii) the requirement to document economic substance and arm's-length transfer pricing where a DTC brand invoices French retail clients while sourcing goods from affiliated non-French suppliers. All cross-border flows are automatically captured by the receiving bank through the SITCO tele-transmission system; no prior regulatory validation is required.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. French law and EU law impose no statutory surrender, no mandatory conversion ratio, and no repatriation deadline for export receivables. A French SAS may retain Shopify Payments, PayPal, Stripe, and direct trade-settlement proceeds indefinitely in EUR or in any foreign currency, at any bank inside or outside the EEA. The sole compliance duty is the annual French foreign-account declaration (déclaration d'un compte détenu à l'étranger) that must be filed with the corporate income-tax return if the company maintains an account with a financial institution outside France.

tier1_domestic_commercial_banks.bank_name: BPCE S.A. (Groupe Banque Populaire et Caisse d'Épargne)

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: High feasibility as an auxiliary treasury rail for remote FX and SEPA-instant payments; low-to-medium as the sole operational bank for a France-based SAS. EEA-licensed Electronic Money Institutions (e.g., Qonto, Manager.One, Payhawk, Airwallex EU entity, or Mangopay) can be onboarded fully virtually, offer French IBANs, and are authorized under PSD2 to hold e-commerce settlement funds. The controlling legal constraints are: (i) client monies held by an EMI are safeguarded under segregation rules but are not covered by the French deposit-guarantee scheme (FGDR); (ii) the EMI must be passported into France and appear in the ACPR register of payment institutions; (iii) documentary trade instruments (Commercial LCs, large SWIFT USD/CNY settlements, import guarantees) require the full balance-sheet credit capacity of a licensed bank and are generally outside EMI product capabilities; and (iv) the treasury must maintain at least one relationship with a tier-1 credit institution for statutory capital, sponsor lines, and regulatory credibility.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: French law does not mandatorily require a physical interview for corporate account opening when the AML identification is achieved through qualified electronic trust services under eIDAS, read with Articles L561-5 and R561-5 of the French Monetary and Financial Code. In practice, tier-1 commercial banks (BNP Paribas, Société Générale, Crédit Agricole) require the legal representative (Président) and ideally one secondary signatory to attend an initial in-person interview at a French branch; banks treat non-resident presidents with elevated scrutiny and frequently condition account opening on a physical visit or on the appointment of a locally resident French director with a certified power of attorney. Remote video-KYC opening is systematically available from fintech EMIs and from the digital arms of the commercial banks (e.g., Qonto, SG's digital onboarding, BPCE's 100% digital professional offering), subject to notarized/apostilled corporate documents and proof of the economic nexus of the DTC activity.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Non-resident beneficial owner or multi-tier foreign holding chain with cumulative UBO ownership above 25%
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Current KBIS extract dated within three months, signed UBO declaration matching the Registre des Bénéficiaires Effectifs (RBE) filing, certified chain-of-title and organizational chart for each intermediate entity, good-standing certificates from the foreign company registers, and apostilled or legalized constitutional documents translated into English/French by a certified translator.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Zero-minimum-capital SAS with a digital-only DTC brand and thin tangible-asset substance
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Shareholders' resolution on the initial capital and share premium, full source-of-funds trail from the shareholder's bank account to the French account, a twelve-month cash-flow and treasury forecast, Shopify and Shopify Payments legal-entity and business-activity verification, brand trademark or IP registration certificates, and executed copies of supplier, logistics, and customer-facing agreements evidencing the operating cycle.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Card-not-present (CNP) e-commerce architecture with high transaction velocity and multi-jurisdiction customer inflows
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: PCI-DSS v4.0 Level 1 attestation of compliance for the acquiring and settlement stack, evidence of PSD2 Strong Customer Authentication through 3-D Secure, chargeback and dispute statistics below 1% over the trailing six months, refund policy documentation, and a reconciliation file matching Shopify settlement reports to bank credits.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Use of a commercial domiciliation address (business incubator or virtual office) and absence of registered office in owned premises
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Notarized or contractual domiciliation agreement with the registered address provider, utility bill or occupancy certificate, the KBIS address, and a written explanation from the Président explaining the e-commerce operational structure including storage, fulfillment, and marketing premises if any.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Foreign tax residency of the legal representative with no French fiscal footprint
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Apostilled or legalized passport, proof of current residential address, a tax-residence certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, personal bank statements or wealth evidence for the source-of-wealth declaration if requested, and a notarized power of attorney appointing a local French signatory to operate the account.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: SWIFT MT103 from the non-resident shareholder's bank to the SAS's EUR operational account at BNP Paribas Paris or Société Générale Paris, with the remittance information field (Field 70) reading 'CAPITAL SUBSCRIPTION - SHARE PREMIUM - INWARD DIRECT INVESTMENT' and the SAS's full legal name and registration number. The receiving bank will map the transaction into the Banque de France SITCO balance-of-payments classification as a direct investment; the company must file the annual declaration of financial relations with non-residents where the cross-border investment relationship reaches the EUR 1,000,000 statutory reporting threshold, and the bank will notify the company if a specific survey or états déclaratifs are triggered. No exchange-control clearance or commercial invoice is required. The evidentiary pack consists of the notarized or electronic shareholders' resolution approving the capital increase, the updated articles of association following the share subscription, the share-register entry, and the bank's own account-opening file confirming the corporate UBO. The funds must remain at the disposal of the company; if placed on a 'compte bloqué' for capital formation, the release instruction must match the registration certificate at the Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: For suppliers within the SEPA zone, SEPA Credit Transfer (SCT) and SCT Inst provide the efficient low-value clearing rail for recurring dropshipping, logistics, and marketing payouts. For non-EEA suppliers, the standard rail is SWIFT MT103 settled in EUR, USD, or CNY, with the material purpose code referencing the underlying supplier invoice; where credit insurance or supplier security is required, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit opened under UCP 600, preferably confirmed by the beneficiary's bank, is the accepted instrument for high-value stock purchases (especially apparel and consumer-goods manufacturing in Asia). The treasury design should also include: (i) a USD sub-account and a CNY sub-account at the French tier-1 bank to avoid double FX conversion on multi-currency receipts from Shopify Payments and to match USD-denominated supplier invoices; (ii) a dedicated vendor-payments calendar that nets SEPA payments twice weekly and schedules SWIFT currency buys when the FX rate reaches the treasury target; and (iii) documentary collection, such as D/P terms, for mid-value transactions where a full commercial LC is economically disproportionate. Open-account MT103 settlements above EUR 250,000 per counterparty should be backed by a standby LC or an export bank guarantee if the supplier is in a higher political-risk jurisdiction.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: FX spot contracts (change au comptant) for immediate conversion of USD, GBP, or CNY e-commerce settlement proceeds into EUR.
Outright currency forwards (change à terme) and optional-date forwards on EUR/USD, EUR/GBP, and EUR/CNY, with maturities aligned to the 30-180 day Shopify settlement and supplier payment cycles.

Non-deliverable forwards (NDF) on currencies without a deliverable EUR market (e.g., INR, BRL, TRY), documented with matching underlying trade or operating-expense exposure to qualify for hedge accounting and to avoid speculative treatment.
FX swaps (swap de change) for rolling working-capital positions, covering the gap between receipt of foreign-currency receivables and the EUR disbursement for duty, VAT, or supplier payments.

Cross-currency interest rate swaps (cross-currency swaps) for intercompany financing or medium-term acquisition funding where the SAS has a EUR asset base and a USD liability, subject to the EMIR non-financial-counterparty clearing threshold being respected.

European-style FX options (call/put with premium) employed exclusively for economic-hedge accounting under IFRS 9, limited to identified residual risk and approved by the board as part of the annual treasury-risk policy.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Annual shareholder approval of statutory financial statements (SAS collective decision; approval of annual accounts)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Shareholders of the SAS (internal decision; minutes recorded in corporate register and kept at registered office)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: No later than six months after the fiscal year end; extension possible by commercial court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to approve within the statutory six-month period exposes the legal representative to court injunction and personal liability risk; the annual accounts cannot be filed on time, and the company loses statutory filing protection.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Filing of annual accounts (comptes annuels) with management report and statutory auditor's report, if any
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: RCS registry via INPI single window (Guichet unique) / Greffe du Tribunal de Commerce
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Within one month after shareholder approval; shareholder approval must occur within six months after fiscal year end unless extended by court order
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Commercial court injunctive order with daily penalty payment (astreinte); persistent non-filing may lead to public prosecutor application for court-ordered strike-off after formal notice.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Corporate income tax result declaration (déclaration de résultats) with tax annexes — Form 2065-SD
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP French tax administration (Service des Impôts des Entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: For a 31 December year end: second working day after 1 May; for other fiscal year ends: within three months of the annual closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing incurs a 10% penalty if regularized within 30 days after formal notice and 40% thereafter; late-payment interest accrues at 0.20% per month; non-payment of assessed tax adds a 5% collection surcharge.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Final corporate income tax balance payment (solde d'impôt sur les sociétés)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP French tax administration (Service des Impôts des Entreprises)
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Payable on the corporate income tax return filing date; for a 31 December year end, the second working day after 1 May; for other year ends, within three months of the annual closing date
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Failure to pay the balance by the due date triggers an automatic 5% penalty on the unpaid amount plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.20%; enforced tax recovery proceedings may follow.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Local business contribution / property-based business tax (Cotisation Foncière des Entreprises, CFE) annual payment and declaration if premises or activity data change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: DGFiP French tax administration and relevant local authority tax collection office
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual tax due by 15 December of the assessment year; annual declaration (Form 1447-C) required only when premises or activity data change; no separate filing if there is no change
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late payment incurs a 5% surcharge plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.20%; continuing arrears may lead to seizure and recovery proceedings against company assets.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: Mandatory appointment of a statutory auditor (commissaire aux comptes) where the SAS exceeds two of three thresholds at the balance sheet date: balance-sheet total greater than EUR 4,000,000; net turnover greater than EUR 8,000,000; average workforce greater than 50 employees. A statutory auditor may also be required on shareholder request (shareholders representing at least one-third of capital) or in a consolidated/group control context.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: French GAAP (PCG / ANC regulatory framework); annual accounts presented in EUR; IFRS permitted only for consolidated financial statements of listed entities under EC Regulation 1606/2002.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: France does not require a separate annual beneficial-owner re-filing. The beneficial-owner declaration (bénéficiaire effectif) is filed with the RCS at incorporation and must be updated within 30 days of any change in beneficial ownership. The UBO register record should be verified annually during the annual accounts approval process; no annual renewal is due if the information is unchanged.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Members (shareholders and share transfer ledger)
Register of Directors (statutory representatives and decision record)
Minute Book (minutes of shareholder decisions and collective meetings)

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.registered_office_or_agent_market_range_: USD 500–1,700 (approximately EUR 460–1,550) for commercial domiciliation / registered agent services and annual secretarial assistance
recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: USD 7,000–18,000 (approximately EUR 6,500–16,500) when a statutory audit is mandatory; below the thresholds, voluntary audit fees typically range from USD 8,000–15,000

corporate_income_tax_regime.statutory_headline_rate: 25% for financial years ending on or after 31 December 2022; previously phased from 33.33% to 28% and then to 25%.
corporate_income_tax_regime.effective_tax_rate_incentives: Reduced 15% rate applies to the first EUR 38,120 of taxable profit for eligible SMEs with turnover below EUR 10 million; Research Tax Credit (CIR) at 30% of eligible R&D expenses; Innovation Tax Credit (CII) at 20% up to EUR 400,000 of eligible innovation expenditure; Young Innovative Enterprise (JEI) exemption regime for qualifying SAS entities; territorial and participation exemptions for certain long-term equity holdings.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.form_identifier_and_portal: Formulaire n°2065-SD (Déclaration de résultats) and annexes n°2051-SD to 2059-SD, filed electronically through the EFI/EDI module of the impots.gouv.fr professional portal; mandatory e-filing applies to all SAS entities subject to corporate income tax.
tax_return_filing_anatomy.statutory_deadline_rule: Within three months after the close of each fiscal year. For a 31 December year-end, the administrative e-filing calendar normally fixes the annual result return and annexes due in May, commonly by 18 May or the next business working day. For a non-calendar fiscal year, the deadline is the same three-month period from the year-end close.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 1 – Company identification and legal form
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Legal name, SIREN/SIRET, registered office, date of incorporation, SAS form, and ISAE/APE business classification.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident corporations acting through a French permanent establishment or a taxable French commercial presence must identify the French registered branch or local establishment; a pure foreign-head-office SAS without PE does not file in this section.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Net accounting profit or loss before tax, established under French GAAP and reconciled with the annual accounts.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Attach French branch accounts for the French PE only; allocate head-office global profit only to the extent attributable to the French permanent establishment under OECD-compliant separate-entity principles.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Taxable profit or tax loss after adjustments for non-deductible expenses, depreciation recapture, provisions, and tax consolidation regime where applicable.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Compute the French-source taxable profit of the PE; disallow head-office notional overheads unless contractually documented and arm’s length; do not deduct distributions to the foreign parent.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Box 4 – Crédits d’impôts et réductions d’impôt
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Research tax credit, innovation tax credit, foreign tax credit, and other statutory tax credits/non-refundable reductions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Only French tax credits attributable to French PE activity may be claimed; foreign withholding tax credits on French-source income are generally not available in this line.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Final corporate income tax computation after applying the reduced SME rate on eligible profit, the 25% standard rate on remaining profit, and all carryforward losses and credits.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Apply the same rate schedule to French PE profit; treaty non-discrimination does not provide for a lower rate in the absence of a specific domestic SME status.

field_by_field_filling_dissection.line_or_box_code: Annexe 2058 – Liste des entreprises liées et opérations intragroupe
field_by_field_filling_dissection.entry_description: Disclosure of transactions with related foreign entities, including shareholder advances, royalty charges, service fees, and purchases/resale transactions.
field_by_field_filling_dissection.non_resident_entry_guidance: Non-resident shareholders and related parties must be reported; transfer pricing adjustments are reviewed by the tax administration if the French PE remunerates a foreign parent or affiliated supplier.

tax_return_filing_anatomy.failure_penalties: Late filing of the corporate income tax return triggers a 10% automatic penalty on the net tax due under Article 1728 of the CGI, plus monthly late-payment interest at 0.20% from the original due date. Deliberate inaccurate declarations trigger a 40% penalty under Article 1729(a); fraudulent maneuvers or abuse of law trigger an 80% penalty under Article 1729(b). Failure to file required annexes is subject to a fixed penalty per missing document, capped at 10% of the assessed tax.

profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.statutory_dividend_wht_rate: 25% statutory withholding tax on gross French-source dividends paid to non-resident corporate shareholders under Article 119bis(2) of the CGI. Non-resident individuals may be subject to the 30% flat tax, comprising 12.8% income tax and 17.2% social levies, subject to treaty. Treaty relief may reduce the rate to 15%, 5%, or 0% depending on the convention, and the EU Parent-Subsidiary Directive may eliminate withholding where the EU parent holds at least 10% for at least 24 months.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.treaty_relief_application_protocol: To invoke a treaty reduction, the beneficial owner must provide a completed French Form 5000/5001 or equivalent tax residence certificate issued by the foreign tax authority, together with a certification of beneficial ownership. Where the reduced rate is invoked at source, the French withholding agent must file a request with the Direction Générale des Finances Publiques before payment. If withholding was applied at the full domestic rate, a refund claim may be lodged with the local tax office within two years from the date of withholding, under Article R*196-1 of the Livre des Procédures Fiscales.
profit_repatriation_and_withholding_tax.cross_border_royalty_and_interest_wht: Royalties: French domestic law applies a 33.33% withholding tax to patent royalties, trademark licenses, know-how, copyright income, and similar intellectual property payments made to non-residents, frequently reduced by tax treaties to 0%, 5%, 10%, or 15%. Interest: France generally imposes no statutory withholding tax on ordinary commercial or bank interest paid to non-residents; interest paid to a controlling foreign shareholder may be recharacterized as a distribution where excessive or under thin-capitalization rules; treaty rates for arm’s length interest are commonly 0%.

transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.tp_documentation_threshold_local_currenc: EUR 400 million consolidated group turnover or total balance-sheet assets triggers the mandatory Local File and Master File requirement under Article L13 AA of the LPF. The Country-by-Country Report threshold is EUR 750 million consolidated group turnover. A standalone Shopify DTC brand below these thresholds is not administratively obligated to prepare full TP documentation, but contemporaneous documentation should be available if intercompany transactions exist.
transfer_pricing_and_economic_substance.economic_substance_doctrine: France does not apply domestic Economic Substance Regulations (ESR) modeled on the offshore regimes, but the anti-abuse doctrine and OECD/BEPS minimum substance standards apply. A French SAS must demonstrate real business purpose, local decision-making, physical premises, personnel, and risk control; an artificial mailbox entity without substance may have its corporate tax residence, permanent establishment, and treaty benefits challenged.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Deliberate understatement of Shopify, Stripe, PayPal, or bank settlement revenue; omission of French-source webstore sales; falsification of accounts; or presentation of fabricated deductible expenses to eliminate the French corporate tax liability.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Reassessment of the full tax deficiency plus late-payment interest; 40% penalty for bad faith, 80% penalty for fraud or abuse of law under Article 1729 CGI; criminal prosecution under Article 1741 CGI carries a fine of up to EUR 500,000 and five years imprisonment, increased to EUR 3,000,000 and seven years where committed by an organized group.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who participate in or direct fraudulent schemes are personally liable for criminal fines and imprisonment; tax authorities may pierce the corporate veil and demand civil recovery against directors for concealed assets; travel bans, freezing orders, and disqualification from management may be imposed.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.infraction_category: Shell Company / Absence of Economic Substance
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Operating a French SAS with no real employees, no registered office, no management activity, and no independent decision-making while routing e-commerce profits to a zero-tax or low-tax jurisdiction through artificial invoices, trademark royalties, or management fees.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Disallowance of intercompany deductions and treaty benefits; adjustment of taxable profit to the arm’s length amount; 80% penalty for abuse of law under Article 1729 CGI; possible application of the General Anti-Abuse Rule under ATAD; the company may also be reported to the OECD as a no-substance entity.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be held civilly liable for the full tax deficit and penalties where the shell arrangement is personal or fictitious; in cases of misuse of corporate assets, directors face criminal liability for abus de biens sociaux; travel restrictions may accompany investigation and prosecution.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Structuring DTC brand profit away from France by paying exaggerated royalties, procurement commissions, or logistics fees to a related foreign affiliate; or financing the French SAS with heavy shareholder debt carrying above-market interest while stripping taxable profit.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Transfer pricing adjustment to the arm’s length outcome under Article 57 CGI and the OECD Transfer Pricing Guidelines; disallowance of excessive interest under thin-capitalization rules; late-payment interest and penalties, including 80% in cases of fraud; cross-border information exchange and mutual agreement procedure risk.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors who sign false transfer pricing documentation or knowingly use sham contracts risk criminal sanctions for forged documents and tax fraud; the tax administration may assert joint and several liability for penalties, and foreign directors may face entry bans or extradition proceedings in aggravated cross-border cases.

fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.triggering_act: Use of undisclosed payment gateway accounts, routing through shell holding companies, structured cash or crypto settlements, failure to maintain accurate beneficial-owner declarations, or handling transactions with sanctioned jurisdictions while claiming French residence and treaty benefits.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.statutory_sanction: Monetary penalties from the ACPR or TRACFIN for breaches of anti-money laundering obligations; criminal money-laundering sanctions under Articles 324-1 et seq. of the French Criminal Code carry imprisonment of up to five years and fines up to EUR 375,000; enhanced penalties for organized laundering and recidivism; Forfeiture of assets obtained from the proceeds.
fatal_compliance_red_flags_and_liabiliti.personal_liability_of_directors: Directors may be prosecuted as principals or accomplices in money laundering, exposing them to imprisonment, personal fines, asset confiscation, and professional disqualification; civil liability for damages caused to third parties and the State is enforceable against personal estates where corporate veil abuse is proven.
